minutes.headline: Assessors begin a multi-year overhaul of neighborhood/waterfront valuation codes unrevised for 20+ years
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed routine exemption, abatement, and Vision Appraisal contract updates, then focused on two larger initiatives: bringing chapter land properties with missing applications or liens back to full value, and launching a multi-year project (with consultant Reena) to overhaul neighborhood and waterfront classification codes that board members said had gone essentially unexamined for over two decades. The board also worked through wording for town meeting warrant articles updating clause 17 and 41D exemption/deferral limits to reflect a long-unadopted cost-of-living adjustment, set tentative future meeting dates, and voted to enter executive session to handle pending abatement and ATB cases.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors began a multi-year project with a consultant to overhaul neighborhood and waterfront valuation classification codes that members said had gone unexamined for more than 20 years.
The board voted to return chapter land properties with no FY2026 application on file to full valuation after notice letters went unanswered.
A further letter will go to properties sold out of chapter land without a new application or lien, requiring them to file or be returned to full value.
The board confirmed the FY2026 overlay reserve figure going to town meeting as submitted.
Staff and the board worked on warrant-article wording to update clause 17 and 41D exemption and deferral limits for a long-unadopted cost-of-living adjustment.

why_it_matters: A rewrite of how neighborhoods and waterfront parcels are classified can shift individual assessments and tax bills once the new codes are adopted.
Owners in chapter land whose applications or post-sale liens are missing face a return to full-value taxation unless they file.
The clause 17/41D warrant article going to town meeting would change exemption and deferral limits for senior and disabled taxpayers.
watch_next: Neighborhood/waterfront classification progress update targeted for the May 21 meeting
Next board meeting tentatively May 5, with May 14 as a backup
